Guide01 Workflow Example: A River-Depth Sensitivity Experiment

This learner manual follows a small, controlled CaMa-Flood sensitivity experiment. The Control run uses the sample Mekong map. The Deep Channel run changes valid rivhgt cells by +3.0 m; all other configured run inputs are kept the same. The workflow prepares that map variant, runs the two 2000 simulations, examines their NetCDF output, and applies the existing one-minute flood-depth downscaler to one selected event.

Before looking at the figures, consider: If the mapped river channel becomes deeper, must river depth, water-surface elevation, discharge, and inundation all increase together? The figures let you examine that question. This is a model sensitivity example, not observational validation or a forecast of a real channel-engineering project.

1. What is being compared?

The rivhgt map parameter is river-channel depth in metres. The model calculates channel-bed elevation from terrain elevation and rivhgt; river water depth and absolute water-surface elevation are distinct quantities. The two runs therefore help illustrate why a change in one variable does not determine the direction of change in another.

The intended difference is the file selected by CRIVHGT:

Case CRIVHGT input
Control Shared sample map, map/mekong_15min/netcdf/rivhgt.nc
Deep Channel Tutorial-local map_modify/rivhgt_deep.nc

Both are one-year cold starts for calendar year 2000, using the Tutorial02 mek_default physics configuration and daily NetCDF output. No prior-year spin-up or Restart is used. The runoff, input matrix, map geometry, and other settings are matched. These choices make the pair a controlled sensitivity comparison, but the one-year cold start limits what can be concluded.

The example is part of Guide01, a contributor workflow example on the development branch. It is not a separately validated production tutorial. For Guide01’s purpose and development workflow, see the Guide01 overview. For the scientific and technical design, see the workflow design. The implementation evidence and unresolved choices are recorded in ../22implementation_record.md.

2. Prepare the repository and inputs

Start at the repository root

Open a terminal and change to the root of your CaMa-Flood checkout. The following commands assume that the checkout contains this Guide01 example. Confirm the location before saving it in a shell variable:

cd /path/to/CaMa-Flood_v4
pwd

The printed path should end in your repository directory. Set cmf_root in the same terminal session:

cmf_root="$(pwd)"
git branch --show-current

cmf_root is a shell variable, not a permanent setting; define it again in a new terminal. This example was implemented on feature/gosh-refactor. If you are using another checkout, first confirm that the Guide01 files and required sample datasets are present.

Inspect the example files

cd "${cmf_root}"
cd tutorial/guide01_how_to_develop_tutorial/workflow_example
pwd
ls -lhF

The scripts are kept directly in the example directory. The directories have separate roles: map_modify/ holds the changed map parameter, out/ holds model runs and downscaling products, analysis/ holds derived tables and NetCDF diagnostics, and figure/ holds plots. design/ contains development records for tutorial authors, rather than steps needed by a learner.

An excerpt from the inspected checkout’s ls -lhF output is:

drwxr-xr-x@ 8 yamadai  staff   256B Nov  9 16:41 analysis/
drwxr-xr-x@ 8 yamadai  staff   256B Nov  9 16:51 figure/
drwxr-xr-x@ 3 yamadai  staff    96B Nov  9 16:37 map_modify/
drwxr-xr-x@ 6 yamadai  staff   192B Nov  9 16:45 out/
-rwxr-xr-x@ 1 yamadai  staff   5.2K Nov  9 16:53 a02-prepare_downscale_input.py*
-rwxr-xr-x@ 1 yamadai  staff   5.5K Nov  9 16:34 s01-prepare_map.py*
[… other entries omitted …]

The * marker indicates an executable in this ls -F listing. Sizes and timestamps can differ in another checkout or after rerunning the workflow.

The sample inputs used by the runner are repository-level files:

  • Mekong map files under map/mekong_15min/netcdf/ and map/mekong_15min/;
  • runoff file inp/test-mek_1deg_nc/runoff2000.nc;
  • input matrix map/mekong_15min/inpmat_test-mek_1deg.bin and its dimension description map/mekong_15min/inpdim_test-mek_1deg.txt.

These are inputs, not files produced by this tutorial. The original rivhgt.nc is read-only. The runner checks for its required inputs before starting a simulation.

Prepare Python and the model executable

The Python workflow uses NumPy, NetCDF4, xarray, pandas, Matplotlib, and the repository’s cmf_colormap package. The recommended environment is the repository .venv:

cd "${cmf_root}"
bash s02-python_setup.sh
source .venv/bin/activate

The setup script is interactive when it needs to create or update the environment; follow its displayed confirmation prompt. In a non-interactive terminal it diagnoses the environment without changing it. See the Python environment guide and the repository setup instructions for the existing-environment and troubleshooting options.

The run scripts expect the NetCDF-enabled executable at out/bin/MAIN_cmf_netcdf. If that file is missing, prepare the compiler configuration described in the v5 build guide, then build the separate NetCDF executable from the repository root:

cd "${cmf_root}"
bash gosh_sample/compile_netcdf.sh

This build requires GNU Make, GNU Fortran, and NetCDF-Fortran tools including nf-config. It writes out/bin/MAIN_cmf_netcdf; it does not run either experiment. The example scripts use the repository .venv interpreter by absolute path, so activate or prepare that environment before running them.

Learning Check

  • Which inputs are shared repository data, and which map file will this example generate?
  • Why should the shared rivhgt.nc remain unchanged?

3. Create the Deep Channel map

Question: How can the experiment change one map parameter without changing the shared map or its missing-cell pattern?

The preparation script reads the shared rivhgt.nc, adds 3.0 m to valid cells, and writes map_modify/rivhgt_deep.nc. It checks the data type, grid, coordinates, missing mask, and increment, and checks that the shared source checksum remains unchanged. The Deep Channel runner later supplies the tutorial-local file directly through CRIVHGT; it does not copy the file into the shared map directory.

Run from the repository root:

cd "${cmf_root}"
./.venv/bin/python tutorial/guide01_how_to_develop_tutorial/workflow_example/s01-prepare_map.py

If the generated file already exists, the script stops instead of replacing it. To deliberately regenerate this tutorial-owned product, add --force:

./.venv/bin/python tutorial/guide01_how_to_develop_tutorial/workflow_example/s01-prepare_map.py --force

The inspected run reported a 120 × 80 Float32 grid, 6,566 valid cells, 3,034 missing cells, and a +3.0 m change on valid cells. It also reported matching grid and missing mask. These are checks of the generated file, not proof that the modified parameter is scientifically preferable.

Figure 1. Shared rivhgt, the tutorial-local +3 m variant, and Deep Channel minus Control. The difference applies to valid map cells; the unchanged missing-cell mask is not a physical zero-depth result.

Learning Check

  • What does the map-generation check verify besides the numeric increment?
  • Where is the modified map stored, and which case reads it?

4. Run the two simulations

Question: Which conditions must be matched to interpret a paired run as a sensitivity comparison?

The two small wrapper scripts select control or deep_channel; both call run-experiment.sh, which writes a case-specific namelist and launches the model from that case’s run directory. The model configuration uses the same 2000 calendar-year period, runoff, input matrix, physics options, and daily NetCDF output. The only intended scientific input difference is CRIVHGT.

From the repository root, run each case once:

cd "${cmf_root}"
sh tutorial/guide01_how_to_develop_tutorial/workflow_example/s02-run_control.sh
sh tutorial/guide01_how_to_develop_tutorial/workflow_example/s03-run_deep_channel.sh

Each run is placed under workflow_example/out/control/ or workflow_example/out/deep_channel/. A successful wrapper prints a [SUCCESS] message. It also checks that all four non-empty NetCDF outputs were created. If a run fails, inspect that case’s console_2000.log and log_CaMa_2000.txt before retrying. The scripts refuse to overwrite existing case output by default. To rerun one case, pass --force to its wrapper; the runner replaces only the known outputs in that case’s directory.

The expected output filenames are:

o_outflw2000.nc
o_rivdph2000.nc
o_sfcelv2000.nc
o_fldfrc2000.nc

For this 2000 leap-year run, each file contains 366 daily records on the sample’s 80 × 120 map grid. The time coordinates are interval ends: the first is 2000-01-02T00:00:00, and the last is 2001-01-01T00:00:00. Each record represents the preceding daily interval. February 29 is included. The model starts from a cold start rather than a prior-year Restart, so initial conditions may influence the results.

The output folders also contain generated namelists, model logs, and a Restart file. These large run products are kept under out/; the repository ignore rules exclude that generated run directory.

Learning Check

  • What is the intended difference between the two namelists?
  • Why do 366 records end at 2001-01-01T00:00:00 for a run covering 2000?

5. Inspect the four model outputs

Question: What does each output variable measure, and is it an interval mean or a snapshot?

File variable Meaning Time interpretation Units
outflw River and floodplain discharge Mean over the daily output interval m³/s
rivdph River-channel water depth Snapshot m
sfcelv Water-surface elevation Snapshot m
fldfrc Flooded fraction of a unit catchment Snapshot fraction (0–1)

Check that both cases contain the four expected files:

cd "${cmf_root}"
cd tutorial/guide01_how_to_develop_tutorial/workflow_example
pwd
ls -lhF out/control
ls -lhF out/deep_channel

For example, the checked Control directory contained the four o_*2000.nc files, input_cmf_2000.nam, log_CaMa_2000.txt, and restart2001010100.nc. File sizes depend on the platform and build. To inspect dimensions, coordinates, and units with the configured Python environment:

An excerpt from the checked ls -lhF out/control output was:

-rw-r--r--@ 1 yamadai  staff   3.0M Nov  9 16:40 o_fldfrc2000.nc
-rw-r--r--@ 1 yamadai  staff   5.2M Nov  9 16:40 o_outflw2000.nc
-rw-r--r--@ 1 yamadai  staff   5.0M Nov  9 16:40 o_rivdph2000.nc
-rw-r--r--@ 1 yamadai  staff   4.9M Nov  9 16:40 o_sfcelv2000.nc
[… other entries omitted …]

Sizes and timestamps are an example from one inspected run; they can vary.

"${cmf_root}/.venv/bin/python" - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import xarray as xr

root = Path("tutorial/guide01_how_to_develop_tutorial/workflow_example/out")
for case in ("control", "deep_channel"):
    for name in ("outflw", "rivdph", "sfcelv", "fldfrc"):
        path = root / case / f"o_{name}2000.nc"
        with xr.open_dataset(path) as ds:
            var = ds[name]
            print(case, name, var.dims, var.shape,
                  "units=", var.attrs.get("units"),
                  "first/last=", str(ds.time.values[0]), str(ds.time.values[-1]))
PY

Figure 2 shows the Control values for all four variables at the selected event. Compare the variables with their time meanings in the table: a daily mean discharge is not the same type of quantity as a water-level snapshot.

Figure 2. Control discharge (outflw, daily interval mean), channel-water depth (rivdph), water-surface elevation (sfcelv), and flooded fraction (fldfrc). The three latter fields are snapshots for the represented day 2000-09-21; their stored interval-end time is 2000-09-22. Color scales are chosen per variable and should not be compared across panels as if they shared one unit.

Learning Check

  • Which field is averaged over a day, and which three are snapshots?
  • What should you compare before subtracting one case’s NetCDF field from the other?

6. Compare river response through time

Question: Does a deeper channel necessarily produce a higher water-surface elevation?

The model’s elevation relationship is

sfcelv = elevtn - rivhgt + rivdph

For corresponding cells in these runs, the +3 m change in rivhgt lowers the calculated bed term. A change in rivdph therefore does not by itself determine the sign of the change in absolute sfcelv. Discharge, river depth, and water-surface elevation can respond differently; this experiment does not isolate a particular hydrodynamic mechanism.

The analysis script selects the nearest valid model cell to each reference coordinate and marks those selections as provisional. Rebuild the analysis tables after the simulations, then inspect analysis/provisional_sites.csv and analysis/provisional_timeseries.csv:

cd "${cmf_root}"
./.venv/bin/python tutorial/guide01_how_to_develop_tutorial/workflow_example/a01-analyze_outputs.py --validate-only
./.venv/bin/python tutorial/guide01_how_to_develop_tutorial/workflow_example/a01-analyze_outputs.py

The first command checks aligned grids and timestamps and reports selected cells. The second writes comparison products. In the checked run, the reference coordinates selected nearest valid cells near Vientiane, Phnom Penh, and Can Tho. Their exact locations and approximate offsets are in the CSV; they should not be treated as surveyed gauge locations. The event is selected from the Control sfcelv peak at the provisional Phnom Penh cell: the checked selection was interval end 2000-09-22, representing September 21. This is a reproducible selection rule, not a claim that it is the most important flood event.

Figure 3. Daily interval-mean discharge and daily snapshot river depth and water-surface elevation for the two cases at the three provisional cells. The selected points are nearest valid catchment cells, not an observational validation dataset. In some locations a deeper channel coincides with increased discharge or channel depth while water-surface elevation decreases; the figure is a case-specific response, not a universal rule.

Learning Check

  • Use the elevation relationship to explain how rivdph could increase while sfcelv decreases.
  • What does “provisional nearest valid cell” mean for interpreting Figure 3?

7. Interpret flooded fraction and area

Question: Is a flooded fraction the same as flooded area?

fldfrc is a fraction for a unit catchment. The example estimates the catchment’s flooded area contribution as

cell_flooded_area = fldfrc × ctmare

Here ctmare is the catchment area in square metres; dividing the product by 1,000,000 converts it to km². Summing selected catchment contributions gives the regional estimate. The script uses a provisional rectangle from 104°E to 108°E and 8°N to 13°N and includes catchments by cell-center coordinates; the east and north boundaries are exclusive. This rectangle is not an official Mekong Delta boundary, and results depend on the region and its boundary-cell rule.

The analysis table analysis/provisional_flooded_area.csv stores the two regional series. The checked event-selection record gives about 38,149 km² for Control and 34,383 km² for Deep Channel in that selected region at the selected event. These are model sensitivity results for this setup and mask, not a general prediction that deeper channels reduce flooding.

Figure 4. Top panels show snapshot fldfrc; middle panels show each catchment’s contribution fldfrc × ctmare in km²; the bottom panel sums contributions in the provisional 104–108°E, 8–13°N cell-center region. The rectangle is an analysis choice, not an authoritative delta outline.

Learning Check

  • What additional quantity is needed to turn fldfrc into an area?
  • Why should the region and cell-selection rule accompany a regional-area number?

8. Read spatial differences and one-minute downscaling

Spatial sensitivity

Question: Does the effect of the map change have the same sign everywhere?

analysis/difference_at_event.nc stores Deep Channel minus Control for the four output fields at the common Control-selected event. Figure 5 uses a symmetric color range clipped at the 98th percentile of absolute values for display. The clipping makes the central spatial pattern easier to see but means the most extreme values can lie beyond the displayed range. A positive color means Deep Channel is larger than Control; a negative color means it is smaller. The inspected fields show spatially mixed responses, so avoid generalizing from a single sign or location.

Figure 5. Event-time Deep Channel minus Control for interval-mean discharge and snapshot river depth, water-surface elevation, and flooded fraction. The common event is selected from Control at a provisional cell. The symmetric display limit is capped at each field’s absolute 98th percentile; colorbar labels identify that cap.

One-minute postprocessing

The example then uses the existing Fortran tributary downscaler. Its input preparation script reads the selected NetCDF rivdph record and the matching static rivhgt, checks their grid, units, and time, and derives floodplain depth as

flddph = max(rivdph - rivhgt, 0)

Missing cells remain unassigned. The adapter writes one little-endian Float32 Binary grid, which is consumed by the existing downscaler along with the sample’s high-resolution map data. This workflow adapts NetCDF model output to the existing Binary downscaler; it does not change the downscaling algorithm or run a separate one-minute hydrodynamic simulation.

The checked event is the same Control-selected event for both cases. Figure 6 uses the requested crop 102–108°E and 9–15°N (360 × 360 pixels at one-minute spacing). The downscaler uses an additional five model-cell buffer around the crop to provide context. The output’s 129,600 pixels include 95,543 assigned and 34,057 unassigned pixels in each case. The large-scale patterns look similar in this view, but no numerical identity or general similarity has been established.

Run from the repository root. On a first run, omit --force:

cd "${cmf_root}"
sh tutorial/guide01_how_to_develop_tutorial/workflow_example/s04-downscale_event.sh

This step needs the two model runs, generated event table, .venv, and existing Mekong one-minute map layers. It builds the existing downscaler locally under the example’s out/bin/ if needed, then writes each case’s input and downscaled output under out/downscaling/. When outputs already exist and you intentionally want to replace them, use:

sh tutorial/guide01_how_to_develop_tutorial/workflow_example/s04-downscale_event.sh --force

To regenerate the six figures from the saved model, analysis, and downscaling products:

./.venv/bin/python tutorial/guide01_how_to_develop_tutorial/workflow_example/v01-plot_results.py

The plotting script reads saved results; it does not rerun the model or downscaler. A checked output-validation run reported 360 × 360 values per case, 95,543 assigned pixels, and depth ranges from 0 to 17.5362 m for Control and 0 to 16.0039 m for Deep Channel. The downscaling is postprocessing based on high-resolution terrain and its assumptions; it is not independent validation.

Figure 6. Downscaled inundation depth in metres for the common event, shown over 102–108°E, 9–15°N. Both panels use the same display scale. Unassigned pixels are masked; the result adds spatial detail but is not an independent one-minute simulation or evidence that either experiment is observationally correct.

Learning Check

  • What does the Python adapter calculate before calling the Fortran downscaler?
  • What additional information does one-minute postprocessing provide, and what does it not validate?

9. Discussion: what can this experiment establish?

Use the figures and CSVs to discuss how the two configurations differ. Keep the interpretation tied to the evidence:

  • River depth and absolute water-surface elevation are different quantities; the rivhgt change enters the elevation relationship directly.
  • Discharge and water-depth responses vary spatially. A deeper mapped channel does not guarantee a uniform response.
  • Flooded fraction is not an area until combined with catchment area, and a regional total depends on the chosen region and mask.
  • Downscaling adds spatial detail through terrain-based postprocessing, not independent hydrodynamic evidence.

No observations were used to validate these simulations. They cover only calendar year 2000, start from a cold start, use provisional reference cells, and calculate regional area over a provisional rectangle. The example does not establish spin-up adequacy, isolate a single physical mechanism, or predict the outcome of a real intervention. Review the design and implementation record before reusing any of these choices in a research analysis.

Learning Check

  • Name two reasons why these results should be described as a sensitivity example rather than as a validated prediction.
  • Which provisional choice would you review first before applying the workflow to a new study, and why?

Reproduce the complete workflow

After the Python environment and executable are ready, the following commands reproduce the workflow in order from the repository root. The first run of each step should not need --force in a fresh example directory.

cd "${cmf_root}"
./.venv/bin/python tutorial/guide01_how_to_develop_tutorial/workflow_example/s01-prepare_map.py
sh tutorial/guide01_how_to_develop_tutorial/workflow_example/s02-run_control.sh
sh tutorial/guide01_how_to_develop_tutorial/workflow_example/s03-run_deep_channel.sh
./.venv/bin/python tutorial/guide01_how_to_develop_tutorial/workflow_example/a01-analyze_outputs.py --validate-only
./.venv/bin/python tutorial/guide01_how_to_develop_tutorial/workflow_example/a01-analyze_outputs.py
sh tutorial/guide01_how_to_develop_tutorial/workflow_example/s04-downscale_event.sh
./.venv/bin/python tutorial/guide01_how_to_develop_tutorial/workflow_example/v01-plot_results.py

The model runs take substantially longer than the inspection and plotting steps. Existing outputs are protected from accidental replacement; use the individual --force options only when deliberately regenerating their products. For detailed evidence, exact selected cells, and unresolved research choices, consult ../22implementation_record.md.
